text:
Brent Burns is 41, in his 23rd NHL season, and still has not missed a game. Last April he became only the second player to skate in 1,000 straight regular-season games, and TSN has already raised the idea that he could finish as the league's all-time ironman. He came into the season with 1,579 games and a 2017 Norris Trophy.

This season is quieter. He has 6 assists and no goals in 21 games on 16 and a half minutes a night, and Colorado is about seven points worse in expected goals share with him on the ice at five on five than without him. The shot still has thunder, his hardest in the top 6% of the league at 96.5 mph, but less than a goal's worth of expected goals says few of his attempts are coming from good ice. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged the same habit last season: lots of volume, not much from the slot.

Last season Evolving-Hockey still had him as a top-50 defenseman, 1.6 wins, mostly from even-strength offense. With Cale Makar out injured, he played 19.4 minutes in the win in Montreal. The streak is the headline; his workload is the hockey story.
